name: fix-platform-expansion-six-targets
body:
Source: supported-platforms said "darwin/arm64 and windows/amd64 required; windows/arm64 conditional; Intel macOS and Linux definitely not supported" (per requirements.note.fix-supported-targets-runners). Inconsistency: that non-goal was wrong — Intel Macs were sold until 2023, and GitHub now offers hosted runners for every target the project cares about (macos-15-intel/macos-26-intel for Intel Mac, ubuntu-24.04/ubuntu-24.04-arm for Linux, windows-11-arm now GA). The repo is private and unreleased (no tag has ever published), so this is a clean redefinition, not a breaking change.

Resolution [with user]: all six targets (darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64, windows/amd64, windows/arm64, linux/amd64, linux/arm64) are now supported, each gated only on "does a GitHub-hosted native runner exist for it right now" — the single conditional rule previously applied only to windows/arm64 now generalizes to all six; none is unconditionally "always" supported anymore. Linux gets no package-manager (Homebrew/Scoop-equivalent) channel, only a direct GitHub Release asset download.

Updated nodes: requirements.requirement.supported-platforms, single-binary, native-ci-verification, github-releases, distribution, homebrew-install, install-docs; domain.service.install-kalide; solution.component.homebrew-formula, native-e2e-ci, release-workflow, install-docs. Added: requirements.requirement.linux-install, solution.component.linux-release-asset (realised-by from domain.service.install-kalide, contained by solution.container.package-channels).

requirements.note.fix-supported-targets-runners, requirements.note.fix-single-binary-targets and requirements.note.distribution-decisions are now further superseded on the target-set question specifically by this note. [with user]
